cases.statement: Two unrelated families: a Chinese family (father P3 and his two children P1, P2; P1 re-reported as patient 7 in 32443356) and a Japanese patient (P39, family F23). All are heterozygous.

people.label: P1 (family 1, proband)
people.key_phenotypes: systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus nephritis; hepatomegaly with liver fibrosis; hypothyroidism; pericardial effusion; fever; no oral, genital or perineal ulcers

quotes.quote: The proband 1 (P1), a 14-year-old Chinese girl, presented with abdominal swelling at the age of 7.
She was diagnosed with hypothyroidism, hepatic fibrosis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Family 1 (31299923): the authors note the phenotypes differ from the classic Behçet-like picture (lupus, liver fibrosis, hypothyroidism, Crohn's disease) and state that WES found no variants in other autoinflammatory genes. 32443356 states no variants in other primary-immunodeficiency or monogenic-SLE genes were found in any of its patients. P39 (40574834) has lupus and Sjögren's features; other genes not reported for her.

quotes.quote: No mutations were detected in other genes associated with autoinflammatory diseases (see the Additional file 1) in two families.
Furthermore, signs of liver and thyroid problems were never reported before in HA20 patients in other studies.
No mutations were detected in P5, and no mutations in other genes associated with primary immunodeficiencies and monogenic SLE were identified in all patients.

segregation.statement: Family 1: three affected carriers (father P3 and his two children P1, P2); WES included all family members shown in Fig. 1 and the variant was not detected in other family members (their number and affection status are not stated in the text). 32443356 adds that the variant was absent in patient 7's grandparents by Sanger sequencing. Family F23 (40574834): only P39 is listed.

quotes.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed in two HA20 families, which included all members in Fig. 1.
WES revealed heterozygous c.559C > T(p.Q187X) mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene (RS:NM_006290) in P1, P2 and P3, while the mutation was not detected in other members in family 1.
In our study, WES revealed that a heterozygous c.559C > T(p.Q187X) mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene cosegregates with the disease in three patients of family 1.
The exon, including 559C>T in the TNFAIP3 gene, was screened by Sanger sequencing in patient 7's grandparents.
The mutation was not identified in her grandparents.

de_novo.statement: In P3 (the father): the authors call the variant de novo. 32443356 states the exon was Sanger-sequenced in patient 7's grandparents (i.e., P3's parents, by the stated relationships) and the variant was not found. Parentage confirmation is not stated. Both grandparents are referred to collectively; the text does not name them individually.

quotes.quote: Therefore, the c.559C > T and c.259C > T mutations were de novo for P3 and P4, respectively.
By sequence analysis in family 1, we found that P3 had this de novo mutation and transmitted it to his children.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense change, predicted p.(Gln187Ter) (batch HGVS). Disease mechanism as stated in the papers: heterozygous loss of function (haploinsufficiency).

quotes.quote: HA20 is a new autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3.

The p.Q187X and p.R87X mutations are both located in OUT domains, which controlled NF-κB signaling by deubiquitinating receptor-interacting protein (RIP) 1, RIP2 and TNF receptor-associated factor (TRAF) [24].
A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).

population_data_in_papers.statement: 31299923 checked ExAC, 1000 Genomes and HGMD but states an absence result only for c.259C>T, not for c.559C>T. 32443356 says all its mutations (which include c.559C>T) 'were all found' in a list of databases that mixes population databases (ExAC, 1000 Genomes) with a disease-mutation database (HGMD), so the statement does not show whether c.559C>T is present in a population database.

quotes.quote: The c.259C > T mutation was not found in the above mutation databases.
They were all found in the above mutation databases.

authors_classification.statement: No variant-level ACMG classification. 31299923 says the variant cosegregates with disease and notes it was reported before (its ref 16); 40574834 gives only a cohort-level statement.

quotes.quote: The mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing, but it was reported by other study [16].
All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: Same person: 32443356 patient 7 (HA20-ID0056) is 31299923 P1; 32443356 says the patient was reported in its reference 18, which is 31299923. The pipeline already merged them.
P39 in 40574834 (Japanese family F23) is a separate family; its source report (reference 22, Imai et al. 2020) is not in the batch.
31299923 says the variant was reported earlier (its reference 16, Duncan et al. 2018), not in the batch; that report may contain further carriers.
P3 (father) refused further assessment, so his phenotype comes from history only.
32443356's population-database sentence covers all its variants together and includes HGMD, so it is not a clean population-frequency statement.
31299923 uses transcript NM_006290 (no version); the batch uses NM_001270508.2.
notes_for_panel: Three-carrier Chinese family with a reported de novo origin in the father (grandparents tested negative) plus one unrelated Japanese carrier. No functional assay of this variant in the batch papers.
